label: accepted

evidence.V1: Front and three-quarter read immediately as a cut-stone wall section with coping and plinth; silhouette and top are a plain slab, which is correct for a tiling 8x2x12 module.
evidence.V2: Clear: big = wall slab, medium = coping cap, plinth course and staggered ashlar blocks, small = chamfered block edges and mortar recesses.
evidence.V3: Clean but stiff: blocks are flat, near-square and evenly inset with little size or bulge variation, and the end face is a plain untreated slab - only partly stylised.
evidence.V4: Every block, the coping and the plinth carry a consistent small chamfer that catches the studio light (face and top close-ups).
evidence.V5: Studio close-ups are clean, but the flat-light end_section close-up shows a faint stair-stepped/speckled line where the block faces meet the end strip, suggesting a coplanar sliver or z-fight between the block shells and the core (139 cross-shell overlaps).
evidence.V6: Disciplined: one stone hue in 3 values (light, mid, dark plinth) with the coping in the light value; colourways (brick, sandstone) keep the same scheme.
evidence.V7: 544 tris vs module target 800 / ceiling 2000 - under target.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, smooth shading, ~0.05-stud chamfers and a 3-value stone hue match the modular kit spec; T1 tiling passes flush on the 2-stud grid.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Box, CanTouch off, CastShadow on, grid-corner pivot for 2-stud snapping, Color white, SmoothPlastic.

artifacts: faint stair-stepped sliver along the block-face / end-strip boundary in flat light (possible coplanar z-fight)
top_fixes: Push the block shells slightly proud of (or inset from) the end strip so no coplanar faces remain at the wall ends
Add variation: a few taller/wider blocks and a slight face bulge or random tilt so the ashlar feels hand-cut rather than gridded
Carry the block pattern or a quoin treatment onto the end faces so exposed wall ends do not read as a plain slab
